MY STORY ADVENTURE

Make a Story Map

Choose a character, imagine a place and plan a story with pictures.

Look, then try.

The explorer in the guide is an example. Invent your own character and something they want. Give them a small problem, then decide what they do and how things finish. Sketch simple pictures first; detailed drawing and perfect spelling are not needed.

Start drawing and writing below

Open the worksheet to print or save

An adult helps cut character cards. Keep small paper scraps away from younger children. You can draw, type or ask a grown-up to write your words.

Use a finger, stylus or mouse in each drawing box. Type below it, or ask a grown-up to write your words. Your work stays in this tab. Save before refreshing or leaving.

ACTIVITY 1

My story idea

Sketch your character in the place where the story starts.

ACTIVITY 2

A problem and an ending

Draw what changes and how your character responds.

Your ideas belong here. There is no score.

What are we learning?

Planning helps connect events so a listener can follow what happens and why.

Prefer a worksheet?

Open the individual cartoon activity sheet to print or save. Use portrait orientation and fit to page.
